newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungarian shares end mixed, BUX index rises.
newsitem.headline: Hungarian shares end mixed, BUX index rises.

text.p: The BUX index of the Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE) firmed on Tuesday as strong dollar, rising Dow Jones and positive corporate news helped Hungarian stocks to gains, traders said.
The BUX index rose 24.07 points to 3,665.96, in a turnover of 1.74 billion forints which traders said was high.
Kalman Schuszter of New York Broker said events on international markets encouraged foreign investors to buy Hungarian shares.

"The dollar firmed some one forint, and this determined the trend... and the other reason was the rising of the Dow Jones," said Kalman Schuszter of New York Broker. "But the futures market looks at this with certain reservations."

BUX index futures rose 10 to 30 points, but Schuszter said the December maturity, which closed at 3,705 points, was hardly above the current value of the BUX, and this does not reflect excessive optimism.
Oil and gas company MOL remained in focus on Tuesday, finishing at 1,820 forints, up 30.

Traders said that after last week's government decision about energy price rises for 1997, MOL was expected to improve its results next year. The market also heard news that MOL found new oil or gas fields near Szeged, southern Hungary, traders added.
Other shares closed mixed, but the gains of some heavy-weight issues, such as drug makers Egis and Richter and salami maker Pick helped the BUX index to rise, traders said.
Dealers said the BSE may continue to rise in the near future, but downward corrections may also come.
"Many people expect the rises to run out of steam," Schuszter said.
"Profit-taking may come at any time," said Istvan Imrich of IBB Securities.
